how:
Data-driven population segments (Shreyas, Nov 15: replace the keyword role labels; groups and subgroups labelled with who they are, what
they likely say and who they likely vote for; keep recalibrating).

DATING: everything uses launches dated before the cut C and reads fetched before C (default: now). Re-run nightly; segments keep stable ids.
1. Groups (taste). People with >= MIN_UP upvotes on launches of the 730 days before C. Features = TF-IDF topic profile (L2) of
   the launches they upvoted (launch co-vote SVD factors were tried and dropped: they grouped people by active weeks, not taste). MiniBatchKMeans, K groups. People with 1..MIN_UP-1 upvotes are assigned to the nearest
   group by their topic profile (flag low_signal). People with no upvote in the window: group "not active in the last 180 days".
2. Subgroups (style, within each group). Standardised [ln(1+upvotes 30d), comment rate, made/hunted a launch, reviews+stacks, follows,
   role keywords (multi-hot; no headline/bio is its own column)]; KMeans with k = 2..4 by group size, each subgroup >= 20 people.
3. Descriptors (computed, aggregate only): size, activity, role mix, share commenting / making, topics by lift vs the whole population,
   products most upvoted (share of the group and lift), and up to 60 of the group's own comments (text matched by comment id from the
   launch-page dump, condensed by Gemini into themes, never quoted).
4. Names: Gemini 2.5 Flash names ALL groups in one comparative call (then each group's subgroups in one call) from the descriptors only,
   told that shared traits (developer / founder / AI) do not distinguish and names must differ; topic-lift fallback if the call fails.
   Stable ids: new centroids are matched to the previous run's (Hungarian, cosine); a matched group keeps its id and name unless its
   descriptors drift (top-10 lifted topics overlap < 5), then it is renamed.
5. Calibration (every run): cut C' = C - 7 days, refit groups on data before C', then for each launch dated in [C', C) with >= 20 held
   backers compare the backers' group mix with (a) the model mix (group sizes x each group's affinity for the launch's topics) and
   (b) the population mix (group shares of upvotes in the 30 days before C'). Metric = mean total-variation distance (lower is better), launch bootstrap. Also: per group, the upvote-rate
   lift on launches whose first topic is one of the group's top-5 lifted topics (does "votes_for" hold out of sample?). Appended to
   history so drift is visible.
Outputs: PRIVATE person -> group/subgroup (salted ids) gs://.../tmp/e5/private/segments/<C>.parquet; PUBLIC (aggregates, groups/subgroups
>= 20 people, no ids/usernames/headlines): results/web/segments/<C>.json and results/web/segments/latest.json; calibration history
results/web/segments/calibration_history.jsonl. Launch topics: warehouse (2026) + H25_SRC daily files (2025) when set.
    H25_SRC=<dir> python population_segments.py <store dir> <cf dir> <scratchpad> [--cut YYYY-MM-DD] [--k 12] [--no-upload] [--no-llm]

groups.name: Social App Enthusiasts
groups.who: These users are active in social media, design, and health & fitness, often engaging with iOS apps and educational tools.
says: They appreciate well-designed, user-friendly apps that solve personal problems or enhance daily life.
They often provide specific feedback on features, usability, and potential improvements.
They express excitement and support for new tools, especially those that simplify complex tasks or offer unique solutions.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products in social media, advertising, health & fitness, iOS, design tools, marketing, and education, with a particular interest in video editing and social connection tools.

subgroups.name: Founder-Marketer Launchers
subgroups.who: These users are founders and marketers, highly engaged with commenting and making launches, showing strong interest in social media, health & fitness, and marketing tools.
says: Announcing their own product launches, often detailing the problem it solves and the technology used.
Expressing excitement and support for new tools that address specific pain points in their workflow.
Asking technical questions about implementation or features of launched products.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in social media, health & fitness, iOS apps, design tools, and marketing, with a particular interest in new AI-powered solutions.

subgroups.name: Student App Users
subgroups.who: These users are primarily students, less engaged in commenting or making launches, and often lack detailed profiles, showing interest in social media, advertising, and games.
says: Expressing enthusiasm and eagerness to try new apps and tools.
Asking practical questions about product availability, trials, or specific features.
Sharing personal experiences with products, often related to health or productivity.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products related to social media, advertising, games, health & fitness, and iOS apps, often seeking tools for personal use or entertainment.

subgroups.name: Designer Creators
subgroups.who: These users are predominantly designers, highly engaged in commenting and making launches, with a strong focus on design tools, user experience, and website builders.
says: Providing constructive feedback on product design, visual identity, and user experience.
Sharing their own creative process and the motivation behind building their products.
Discussing the importance of aesthetics and clarity in product presentation.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in social media, health & fitness, iOS apps, design tools, website builders, and user experience, with a keen eye for visual quality and innovative creation tools.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

groups.name: Productivity & Wellness Seekers
groups.who: This segment consists of users interested in personal well-being, productivity, and efficient digital tools, often with a product or marketing background.
says: They value tools that streamline workflows, enhance focus, and improve personal organization.
They are keen on privacy and data security, especially for health and personal data.
They often share their personal experiences with similar tools and suggest how new products could integrate into their existing routines.
groups.votes_for: They support products related to health & fitness, Chrome extensions, iOS/Android apps, user experience, task management, education, and general productivity, with a focus on tools that help manage time and information.

subgroups.name: Student Wellness Seekers
subgroups.who: This segment consists of users with a student role, showing lower engagement in commenting and making launches, and a higher likelihood of not having a headline or bio.
says: They express curiosity about product functionality, asking practical questions about features, limitations, and potential improvements.
They share personal experiences and needs, often highlighting how a product could solve a specific problem they face.
They show excitement for new tools, particularly those that promise to enhance productivity or personal well-being.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products related to Chrome Extensions, Health & Fitness, Task Management, and mobile operating systems like Android and iOS, often with an educational focus.

subgroups.name: Engaged Founder-Designers
subgroups.who: This segment is highly engaged, with a significant share of users commenting and making/hunting launches, often identifying as founders or designers.
says: They frequently provide constructive feedback and ask detailed questions about product mechanics, data handling, and potential use cases.
They share their own experiences building products, often introducing their own launches or relating to the challenges of product development.
They express appreciation for innovative concepts and efficiency improvements, often highlighting how a product streamlines workflows or solves a common pain point.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in Health & Fitness, Chrome Extensions, iOS, User Experience, and Task Management, with distinctive interest in specific apps like Cal.com Companion Apps and PlanEat AI.

subgroups.name: Marketing & Design Influencers
subgroups.who: This segment shows high engagement in reviews and follows, with a strong representation of marketers and designers, and no users lacking a headline or bio.
says: They offer praise and congratulations on launches, often mentioning specific features they find impressive or useful.
They ask about future features, integrations, and scalability, indicating a forward-thinking and strategic perspective.
They share insights from their professional experience, particularly in consumer research and marketing, relating products to real-world business challenges.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in Health & Fitness, Chrome Extensions, iOS, User Experience, and Education, with distinctive interest in tools like Lexie and ManyPI.

subgroups.name: Product Manager Innovators
subgroups.who: This segment has a very high lift for the 'product' role, showing strong engagement in commenting and making/hunting launches, and no users without a headline or bio.
says: They discuss the underlying philosophy and problem-solving approach of products, often relating it to user experience and the challenges of prompt engineering.
They ask detailed questions about product functionality, scalability, and potential use cases, often from a builder's perspective.
They express excitement for innovative solutions that address real-world pain points, particularly in areas like automation, data management, and team collaboration.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products in Health & Fitness, Chrome Extensions, iOS, User Experience, and Design Tools, with distinctive interest in apps like Music AI Bubble and Droppable.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

groups.name: Investor & Business Strategists
groups.who: This group includes investors and founders focused on business growth, sales, and data-driven decision-making, particularly within SaaS and Fintech.
says: They are interested in how AI agents can solve complex business problems, especially in sales, CRM, and data analysis.
They often inquire about the practical implementation, scalability, and integration of business tools.
They share insights from their own entrepreneurial and investment experiences, looking for solutions that offer clear business value.
groups.votes_for: They upvote products in CRM, Fintech, sales, data & analytics, SaaS, e-commerce, and general tech, showing a strong preference for tools that enhance business operations and financial management.

subgroups.name: Engaged Investor-Founders
subgroups.who: This segment consists of highly engaged investors and founders, often with marketing backgrounds, who actively participate in the Product Hunt community by commenting and launching products.
says: They frequently congratulate teams on launches and express excitement to try new products.
They ask insightful questions about product features, development process, and business models.
They share their own experiences and use cases, sometimes promoting their own products or services.
subgroups.votes_for: They show strong interest in CRM, Fintech, and Sales tools, as well as SaaS and Software Engineering products, with specific attention to products like Skarbe and Fundraisly.

subgroups.name: SaaS & Data Strategists
subgroups.who: This segment comprises users interested in business strategy, data, and e-commerce, who are less active in commenting or launching compared to other groups.
says: They inquire about product differentiation and effectiveness compared to competitors.
They share their perspectives as founders or stakeholders, often highlighting the value proposition of a product.
They express interest in free trials and practical applications of new tools.
subgroups.votes_for: They prioritize CRM, Fintech, Sales, and Data & Analytics products, alongside SaaS and E-Commerce solutions.

subgroups.name: Silent CRM & Sales Observers
subgroups.who: This segment is characterized by a high proportion of users without headlines or bios, indicating a more passive engagement style, primarily observing launches related to CRM and sales.
says: They share personal experiences and testimonials about using specific products, often highlighting efficiency gains.
They ask practical questions about product functionality, integration, and potential limitations.
They express appreciation for products that simplify complex business processes or provide transparency.
subgroups.votes_for: They are highly focused on CRM, Fintech, Sales, and Customer Communication tools, with a notable interest in products like Katalyst and Lightfield.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

groups.name: Growth & Marketing Innovators
groups.who: These users are highly active marketers and product managers who are keen on no-code solutions, sales, and leveraging AI for growth.
says: They are interested in tools that accelerate growth experiments, automate marketing tasks, and improve customer engagement.
They often discuss the practical application of AI in marketing, sales, and content creation.
They value products that offer clear benefits in terms of efficiency, output quality, and strategic advantage.
groups.votes_for: They favor products in no-code development, sales, SaaS, marketing, social media, artificial intelligence, education, and video, with a strong emphasis on AI-powered growth and content generation tools.

subgroups.name: Marketing & Sales Strategists
subgroups.who: These are highly engaged marketers with a strong interest in sales, no-code, and social media, often involved in making or hunting launches.
says: They inquire about the practical implementation and safeguards of AI tools, especially regarding automation and data handling.
They express curiosity about how products integrate into existing workflows and cater to non-technical users or solo builders.
They appreciate innovative concepts and user-friendly interfaces, often providing specific feedback on features like editing or data updates.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products that offer practical solutions for sales, marketing, and no-code development, with a focus on AI-powered tools for efficiency and creative direction.

subgroups.name: No-Code & SaaS Enthusiasts
subgroups.who: This segment consists of less active users, including students, who are interested in no-code, sales, and SaaS solutions, with a lower rate of commenting or making launches.
says: They are interested in the technical aspects of products, such as processing speed, platform compatibility, and data security.
They often ask about specific use cases and how products solve common pain points in design, development, or recruitment.
They appreciate minimalist design, open-source initiatives, and tools that offer a more intuitive or integrated experience.
subgroups.votes_for: They support launches in no-code, sales, and SaaS, particularly those that leverage AI for efficiency, improve workflows, or offer innovative solutions for common business and development challenges.

subgroups.name: Founder-Makers & Innovators
subgroups.who: This group comprises highly active founders, developers, and designers who frequently make or hunt launches, focusing on no-code, sales, and marketing tools.
says: They praise innovative features that solve specific pain points, especially in AI-powered content generation and workflow automation.
They express interest in the underlying technology and potential for integration, often asking about APIs or multiplatform support.
They offer congratulations and encouragement to other makers, often sharing their own experiences or insights related to product development.
subgroups.votes_for: They favor products that push the boundaries in no-code, sales, and marketing, especially those offering advanced AI capabilities for video, voice, and data analysis, often with a focus on developer tools and agent development.

subgroups.name: Product Managers & Designers
subgroups.who: This small but highly engaged group consists primarily of product managers, designers, and developers who are active in making launches and deeply interested in data analysis and design tools.
says: They appreciate tools that streamline data analysis, especially those that move beyond dashboards to provide direct answers and insights.
They are concerned about data privacy and security, particularly when using AI agents for sensitive information.
They value visual thinking tools, local processing for confidentiality, and products that significantly improve UI/UX or product development workflows.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote launches in sales, no-code, and SaaS, with a strong preference for design tools, data intelligence platforms, and AI agents that enhance productivity, research, and visual organization.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

groups.name: Mac & Design Aficionados
groups.who: This segment comprises designers and Mac users who prioritize user experience, productivity, and native macOS applications.
says: They appreciate minimalist design, intuitive interfaces, and tools that integrate seamlessly into the Apple ecosystem.
They often share personal pain points related to their digital workflows and seek solutions that simplify their daily tasks.
They are concerned with privacy and local processing, especially for personal data and creative work.
groups.votes_for: They upvote menu bar apps, Mac-specific tools, Apple products, iOS apps, health & fitness, user experience, task management, and productivity tools, with a clear preference for well-designed macOS utilities.

subgroups.name: Designer Makers
subgroups.who: This segment consists primarily of designers who are highly engaged, frequently making or hunting launches, and actively commenting.
says: They often introduce themselves as makers or hunters, sharing their personal journey and motivation behind building the product.
They provide detailed feedback, suggest new features, and engage in technical discussions about product implementation.
They appreciate products that solve real-world problems and improve workflows, often sharing their own experiences with similar challenges.

subgroups.name: Silent Mac Enthusiasts
subgroups.who: This segment comprises users who are less active in commenting or making, often lacking a headline or bio, but show strong interest in Mac-related products.
says: Their comments are often brief, expressing excitement or simple observations about the product's potential.
They occasionally share personal anecdotes about using similar tools or their initial impressions of a new product.
They sometimes inquire about specific features or compatibility, particularly regarding local AI models or integration with existing workflows.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote Menu Bar Apps, Mac, Apple, and iOS products, also showing interest in Health & Fitness, User Experience, Writing, and Task Management tools.

subgroups.name: Engaged Mac Users
subgroups.who: This segment is highly engaged in commenting, with a significant portion also making or hunting launches, and they are particularly interested in Mac and iOS applications.
says: They frequently congratulate makers on their launches and express enthusiasm for new products.
They often share how they plan to use the product or how it addresses a personal pain point.
They engage in discussions about product features, suggest improvements, and compare new tools to existing solutions.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote Menu Bar Apps, Mac, Apple, and iOS products, with a focus on Health & Fitness, User Experience, Productivity, and Task Management tools.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

subgroups.who: This segment consists of founders and product people who are actively engaged in building and launching products, often with a focus on developer tools and AI agent orchestration.
says: They discuss technical implementation details of AI agents, cloud infrastructure, and integration challenges.
They share their own experiences with similar tools and offer constructive feedback or feature suggestions.

subgroups.votes_for: They upvote products related to YC applications, developer tools, AI agent orchestration, and practical solutions for common founder/admin problems like scheduling and lead generation.

groups.votes_for: They upvote products in open source, GitHub, software engineering, developer tools, APIs, and general tech, with a strong preference for tools that support efficient and secure software development workflows.

subgroups.name: Developer Collaborators
subgroups.who: This segment consists primarily of developers and product managers who are highly engaged with open-source projects and developer tools, often contributing to or making launches themselves.
says: They frequently offer detailed technical feedback and suggestions for new features, often from the perspective of a user or a maker.
They share their own experiences using the product or similar tools, highlighting real-world applications and benefits.
They express excitement and support for new launches, often introducing themselves as makers or team members.
subgroups.votes_for: They back launches related to open-source software, GitHub, software engineering, developer tools, and APIs, with a focus on practical utility and problem-solving.

subgroups.name: Open Source Enthusiasts
subgroups.who: This segment is characterized by a strong interest in open-source and developer tools, but with lower engagement in commenting or making launches, and a high proportion of users without detailed profiles.
says: They often give concise positive feedback and express excitement for new products.
They inquire about technical details, especially regarding local-first functionality, on-device processing, and open-source aspects.
They sometimes offer suggestions for improvements or ask about scalability and enterprise applications.
subgroups.votes_for: They primarily upvote open-source projects, GitHub-related tools, software engineering solutions, and developer APIs, showing a preference for tools that are local or offer transparent development.

subgroups.name: Founder-Makers
subgroups.who: This segment is highly active in commenting and making launches, with a significant number of founders, focusing on practical solutions for development workflows and cloud management.
says: They frequently introduce themselves as makers, explaining the problem their product solves and inviting feedback.
They provide in-depth technical questions and suggestions, often relating to integration, performance, and specific use cases.
They share their own pain points and experiences that led to the creation of their products, emphasizing efficiency and streamlined workflows.
subgroups.votes_for: They support launches in GitHub, open-source, software engineering, and developer tools, with a particular interest in products that simplify development environments, manage cloud resources, and enhance productivity.

subgroups.name: Student Developers
subgroups.who: This small but highly engaged segment consists predominantly of students and developers, showing high upvote activity and a strong interest in open-source AI agents and developer tools.
says: They express gratitude for free and open-source tools, often mentioning their utility for school projects.
They ask detailed questions about business models, technical implementation, and how products handle complex scenarios like agent coordination or error handling.
They share personal anecdotes about challenges in development or learning, highlighting how the product addresses those issues.
subgroups.votes_for: They are keen on launches related to GitHub, open-source, developer tools, and software engineering, with a notable focus on AI agents and tools that simplify complex development tasks, especially those beneficial for learning and personal projects.

calibration.note: upvote rate on last week's launches in this group's top topics vs its rate elsewhere, relative to everyone else (1 = no signal); groups fit on data up to 7 days earlier

groups.name: API & AI Development Enthusiasts
groups.who: This segment includes developers and students focused on API development, software engineering, and leveraging AI for autonomous agents and workflow automation.
says: They are interested in tools that simplify API integration, enhance AI agent capabilities, and automate complex development tasks.
They often discuss the security, scalability, and practical application of AI in various development contexts.
They appreciate products that offer simplicity, efficiency, and robust solutions for building and deploying AI-powered applications.
groups.votes_for: They support products in development, APIs, software engineering, open source, developer tools, GitHub, audio, and artificial intelligence, with a focus on tools that enable advanced AI and API-driven solutions.

subgroups.name: Founding Makers
subgroups.who: This segment consists of highly engaged founders and developers who actively create and launch products, often with a strong focus on open source and developer tools.
says: They introduce themselves and their product, explaining the 'why' behind their creation.
They offer technical insights into their product's development and unique features.
They express enthusiasm for new products and congratulate other launchers, often cross-promoting their own launches.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote launches related to Development, Software Engineering, API, Open Source, and Developer Tools, with a particular interest in products that solve real-world problems for builders.

subgroups.name: Agent Workflow Evaluators
subgroups.who: This segment comprises users who are interested in the practical application and evaluation of AI agents, particularly in workflow automation and data analysis, but are not actively launching products themselves.
says: They inquire about the specific problems a product solves and for whom.
They ask detailed questions about technical implementation, such as how AI models handle complex data or maintain context.
They share their experiences using products, highlighting what works well and suggesting improvements.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote launches in Development, API, Software Engineering, and Developer Tools, with a strong emphasis on products that leverage AI for automation, data analysis, and agent-based solutions.

subgroups.name: Under-the-Radar Developers
subgroups.who: This segment includes developers who are less visible on the platform, often without public profiles, but are deeply interested in cutting-edge developer tools and AI agent capabilities.
says: They ask practical questions about product functionality, pricing, and integration with existing systems.
They express interest in how products address common pain points in coding and agent management.
They share personal experiences and insights related to using developer tools and AI agents.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote launches focused on Development, API, Software Engineering, and Developer Tools, with a specific interest in products that enhance coding efficiency, agent security, and system monitoring.

subgroups.name: Student Developers
subgroups.who: This segment is primarily composed of student developers who are highly engaged with new technologies, particularly those that enhance their learning and development workflows.
says: They express excitement about new concepts and potential applications of products.
They ask about product features, integrations, and future development plans.
They share their experiences using products for learning and project development, often suggesting improvements.
subgroups.votes_for: They upvote launches in Development, Software Engineering, Open Source, and Developer Tools, with a notable interest in products that facilitate learning, improve coding efficiency, and offer innovative AI applications.

accuracy_label: Segments are clusters of real held Product Hunt users by what they upvoted in the 180 days before the cut and how they engage (aggregates only, every group and subgroup >= 20 people). Names and 'says' are Gemini summaries of the measured statistics and the members' own comments, not quotes. 'votes_for' is checked out of sample every run (calibration).
